attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his Substack post, in his own voice. It is not a quote of Smith, Elson or Polymarket.

semantics.note: It keeps 'not as kind' and the three named factors. 'With' reads as factors that contributed, so calling it causal is reasonable. The language is firm, not hedged.

contract.note: Marcus named no measure. Reading this as 'less favourable business conditions, with the three factors contributing' is fair and ordinary. Ending June at the June 26 publication date is reasonable. Because 'not as kind' is vague, the result depends on interpretation.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own June 12 record that it pulled Fable/Mythos access under a government directive. It confirms the pause happened, but not its commercial effect or the overall comparison.
A Ramp editorial (June 3) saying a cost-efficiency pullback is starting. It is an assessment, not a measurement of Anthropic usage or revenue.

Vercel gateway data for all of June: Anthropic's spend share is below May but in line with April, and Chinese-model usage is rising. It is one platform's sample, priced at list rates, and covers all of June, so it is not company-wide and shows no causation.

Ramp, all of June: Anthropic's business adoption rose, and Chinese models do not appear to be replacing it. This cuts against displacement as a mechanism, but it measures adoption, not overall business conditions.

reviews.rationale: Only the Fable pause is firmly established (e1). Nothing in the packet shows company-wide business conditions in June were worse than in April and May. Vercel's spend share is down from May but level with April, and Ramp shows Anthropic's adoption rising. No item measures the effect of less tokenmaxxing, and the Chinese-model mechanism is challenged. Neither the support condition nor the contradiction condition is met.
